mcqs.q: In the diagnostic process, examination is which step?
opts: Step II — after taking the history
It is not part of the process
mcqs.explain: Examination is step II of the diagnostic process, following the taking and recording of the patient's history.

mcqs.q: The examination has three components:
mcqs.explain: Examination components are general, extra-oral and intra-oral.

mcqs.q: The four principles of examination are:
mcqs.explain: The principles of examination are inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation.

mcqs.q: 'Palpation' means examining by:
opts: Feeling the tissues with the fingers
mcqs.explain: Palpation is feeling the tissues with the fingers; inspection is visual, percussion is tapping, auscultation is listening.

mcqs.q: 'Percussion' in dental examination refers to:
mcqs.explain: Percussion is tapping the tooth; it can be vertical or lateral/horizontal.

mcqs.q: Intra-oral SOFT-tissue examination includes the:
mcqs.explain: Intra-oral soft-tissue examination covers the gingiva, periodontium and mucosa; hard-tissue examination covers the teeth, occlusion and charting.

mcqs.q: Which instruments belong in the diagnostic kit for charting?
opts: Mouth mirror, probe, explorer, tweezer and periodontal probe
mcqs.explain: The diagnostic kit contains a mouth mirror, straight probe, tweezer, explorers, periodontal probe, gauze, saliva ejector and metal scale, plus blue/red/black pencils.

mcqs.q: Which mucosal structure is inspected during the soft-tissue examination?
opts: Labial/buccal mucosa, palate, tongue and parotid duct
mcqs.explain: Mucosal inspection covers labial & buccal mucosa, parotid duct, palate, uvula/tonsils, tongue, vestibule and frenal attachments.

mcqs.q: When assessing the gingiva, you record its size, colour, consistency, texture, contour and:
mcqs.explain: Gingival/periodontal status: size, colour, consistency, texture, contour, bleeding on probing and pockets.

mcqs.q: Teeth are numbered using the:
mcqs.explain: The FDI two-digit system numbers each tooth by quadrant (permanent 18→28/48→38; deciduous 55→65/85→75).

mcqs.q: Which is assessed under the HARD-tissue (teeth) examination?
opts: Dentition type, occlusion, caries, wear and mobility
mcqs.explain: Teeth examination records dentition type, present/absent teeth, occlusion (Angle's), developmental disorders, caries, attrition/abrasion/erosion, stains and mobility.

mcqs.q: Occlusion is classified using:
mcqs.explain: Occlusion is recorded using Angle's classification and tooth position.

mcqs.q: Dental and periodontal charting is best described as a:
opts: Diagrammatic representation of findings using colour-coded symbols
A written essay of the visit
mcqs.explain: Charting is a diagrammatic representation of dental findings — a quick, accurate record using colour-coded symbols.

mcqs.q: In charting, which colour indicates conditions NOT requiring treatment?
mcqs.explain: Blue = conditions not requiring treatment/intervention; red = intervention required; black = gingival line.

mcqs.q: Which colour indicates that intervention (investigation/treatment) is required?
mcqs.explain: Red indicates intervention (further investigation or treatment) is required.

mcqs.q: The BLACK colour in charting is used for:
mcqs.explain: Black is used for the gingival line (margin/mucogingival junction).

mcqs.q: Dental caries is charted in:
mcqs.explain: Dental caries requires intervention, so it is charted in red.

mcqs.q: A completed root canal filling is charted in:
mcqs.explain: A root-canal-filled tooth is charted in blue (it does not need intervention); periapical pathology, however, is red.

mcqs.q: An amalgam restoration is charted by:
opts: Outlining and shading it in blue
mcqs.explain: Amalgam: outline then shade in blue. Tooth-coloured (composite): outline in blue, do not shade.

mcqs.q: A restoration that is present but needs replacement is shown as:
opts: Solid blue with a red outline
mcqs.explain: Restorations present but needing replacement are coloured solid blue with red outlines.

mcqs.q: Periapical pathology is charted in red ONLY:
opts: After it is seen on a radiograph
mcqs.explain: Periapical pathology is charted in red only after it is confirmed on a radiograph.

mcqs.q: Horizontal mobility of 1–2 mm bucco-lingually is graded:
mcqs.explain: M1 = 0.5–1 mm horizontal; M2 = 1–2 mm horizontal; M3 = vertical mobility or >2 mm horizontal.

mcqs.q: Vertical mobility, or more than 2 mm horizontal mobility, is graded:
mcqs.explain: M3 = mobility in the vertical direction or more than 2 mm horizontal mobility.

mcqs.q: A 'provisional diagnosis' is the process by which the practitioner:
opts: Distinguishes one diagnosis from another (normal vs abnormal)
Confirms the diagnosis with all data
mcqs.explain: A provisional (working) diagnosis distinguishes one diagnosis from another and differentiates normal from abnormal.

mcqs.q: A 'differential diagnosis' is:
opts: A list of several disorders with similar findings from which the correct one is selected
mcqs.explain: A differential diagnosis is a list of disorders with similar histories/physical findings, from which the correct diagnosis is ultimately chosen.

mcqs.q: The FINAL diagnosis is confirmed based on:
opts: History, examination and the results of investigations
mcqs.explain: The final diagnosis is a confirmed diagnosis based on all available data — history, examination and investigation results.

mcqs.q: Phase I (etiotropic / cause-related) therapy includes:
opts: Patient education, plaque control and scaling & root planing
mcqs.explain: Phase I (etiotropic) eliminates etiologic factors: patient education, plaque control, SRP, correcting local factors and controlling risk factors.

mcqs.q: Phase IV of the treatment plan is the:
mcqs.explain: Phase IV is supportive periodontal therapy (maintenance) — periodic recall (3–6 months) to prevent recurrence.

mcqs.q: The conclusion of the examination is summarised by 'SOAP', which stands for:
mcqs.explain: SOAP = Subjective symptoms, Objective symptoms, Assessment, and Plan (record of procedures).

mcqs.q: Extra-oral examination of the neck (shown here) mainly assesses the:
mcqs.explain: Extra-oral examination inspects and palpates the face, TMJ and lymph nodes before intra-oral examination.

mcqs.q: Examining the dorsum, ventrum and borders applies to the:
mcqs.explain: The tongue is examined on its dorsum, ventrum and borders, along with the floor of the mouth.

mcqs.q: Which finding is charted in RED?
mcqs.explain: Overhangs, furcation involvement, recession, caries and fractures all require intervention and are charted in red; a diastema is blue.

mcqs.q: A completely missing third molar WITH a history of extraction is charted as:
mcqs.explain: A missing tooth with a history of extraction is marked X in blue (no intervention needed); without a history of extraction it is marked in red.

saqs.q: List the four principles of examination.
Name the contents of the diagnostic (charting) kit.
saqs.a: Mouth mirror, straight probe, tweezer, explorers, periodontal probe, gauze sponges, saliva ejector, metal scale, plus blue, red and black colour pencils.

saqs.q: State the meaning of each colour in dental charting.
saqs.a: BLUE = conditions NOT requiring treatment/intervention. RED = intervention (investigation/treatment) required. BLACK = the gingival line.

saqs.q: Describe the tooth-mobility grades M1, M2 and M3.
saqs.a: M1 = 0.5–1 mm horizontal; M2 = 1–2 mm horizontal (bucco-lingual); M3 = mobility in the vertical direction or more than 2 mm horizontal.

saqs.q: Differentiate provisional, differential and final diagnosis.
saqs.a: Provisional = distinguishes one diagnosis from another (normal vs abnormal). Differential = a list of disorders with similar findings from which the correct one is selected. Final = the confirmed diagnosis based on history + examination + investigations.

saqs.q: List the four phases of the treatment plan.
saqs.a: Phase I — Etiotropic (cause-related: education, plaque control, SRP). Phase II — Surgical. Phase III — Restorative/corrective. Phase IV — Supportive/maintenance (3–6-month recall).
Subjective symptoms, Objective symptoms, Assessment (when the patient first comes), and Plan (record of the procedures carried out).
